newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday in response to buying by provident funds in otherwise quiet trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 104.33
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 to 103.46
Volume was a moderate 138 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in the Makam.

"The market was very quiet today. The only active players were the provident funds. The funds continue to post net inflows and they need to invest the money in bonds," said Roy Meir of Simodan Brokerage House.

"CPI-linked long bonds continued rising but on relatively low volume," said Eyal Kolka of Sigma Securities. "Yields on inflation-linked bonds have fallen over the last six months from 5.25 percent to 4.1 percent and they are less attractive now."
Unlinked bonds were today's main gainers but volume was low, traders said.
"The market has reached an equilibrium and is expected to remain stable at the current level," Meir said.
Kolka added that despite the rise in prices for unlinked bonds yields remained unchanged.
Makams also rose on volume of 71 million shekels, but traders noted that they usually rose after the weekend.
Dollar-linked bonds fell sharply following the decline of the dollar on overseas markets over the weekend.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
